requirements.text: The cloud/ Worker workspace owns all Cloudflare runtime implementation under cloud/src/cloudflare/. Application packages (shared, server, cli, mcp-server, src) reach the cloud service only through pure contracts in @mdt/domain-contracts and JSON/HTTPS. The cloud package imports only @mdt/domain-contracts; it never imports filesystem-aware shared, server, cli, mcp-server, or src. The main application never imports @mdt/cloud.
Concurrent create requests for one cloud project return unique ticket numbers with no duplicate ticket rows
Concurrent requests sharing one idempotency key return one stable reservation and advance the counter once
Different cloud projects allocate ticket numbers independently
A failed local Markdown write can retry the same reservation and acknowledge it without number reuse
Existing Markdown tickets remain readable and editable during a cloud outage while new cloud-bound creation stays blocked
A real Access-protected environment validates browser and interactive CLI human attribution from a verified email claim
A real Access-protected environment validates service-token machine attribution from a verified common_name claim
Viewer, contributor, and owner permissions are enforced per cloud project for read, reserve, publish, list-members, and manage-members operations
Unauthorized or unknown project references do not disclose project existence; they return the same response as a hidden project
Revoked membership blocks the next protected project operation; there is no authorization cache in the first slice
Acknowledged tickets expose only the approved header projection, never a ticket body
Stale projection writes are rejected through expected-version precondition semantics
The board distinguishes cloud-projected state from canonical local ticket state without implying teammate ownership, presence, or canonical local content
Allocation, projection, membership, denial, and recovery actions produce structured redacted audit records
Disabling cloud binding leaves all durable ticket content usable from Markdown/Git
Reusing one idempotency key with a different canonical request hash returns 409 idempotency_key_reused and does not allocate a new number
Acknowledgement lost after allocation leaves a recoverable reservation that replays with the same reservation id; if abandoned it is marked orphaned and the number is never reused
A scheduled handler marks reserved rows older than 24 hours as abandoned in bounded batches without decrementing the counter or deleting the reservation
The final owner cannot be removed or demoted; a principal cannot grant a role higher than its own
On an unknown kid the Access verifier refreshes JWKS once and retries so key rotation does not require a deployment
Headless adapters refuse to attach service-token headers to any origin not on the operator-controlled allowlist and reject redirects

The coordination database is authoritative for project UUID, membership, ticket-number counter, reservations, idempotency outcomes, projection versions, and audit. Markdown/Git is authoritative for ticket body and projected headers. D1 never writes a projected value back into Markdown.
Ticket numbers are never reused. Abandoned, orphaned, and acknowledged reservations all retain their numbers. The counter is monotonic.
Cloud binding is opt-in per project, enabled only after project provisioning and a successful identity/membership probe.

No Access token, service-token ID/secret, JWT, team domain, or audience tag is permitted in .mdt-config.toml or the global project registry; credentials live only in interactive or backend secret providers.
Rate limiting is only an abuse guard; it must not be used to issue numbers, enforce quotas, or replace D1 unique constraints.
The first slice excludes presence, activity indicators, offline allocation, body sync, WebSockets, and Durable Objects.

The effective trusted-origin set combines distribution-provided HTTPS origins with global fileOnly cloudSync.allowedOrigins extensions; an empty extension list denies custom origins, project files cannot expand trust, and a shipped service does not require per-device project activation.

A cloud-bound create fails recoverably when coordination is unavailable; it never allocates a local fallback number, temporary key, offline range, or lease. This MUST hold through the real TicketService.createCR path (strategy selection), not only the isolated allocator unit test.

Local-only projects behave exactly as before this feature; allocation, creation, and board behavior are unchanged. This MUST be proven with the cloud strategy seam wired into TicketService (a project with no [project.cloudSync] binding selects LocalTicketNumberAllocator and never makes a cloud call).

Another authorized client sees projected create and status changes within the configured polling interval, proven end-to-end (a local projection poller observing the cloud feed), not only the cloud polling endpoint in isolation.

scenarios.title: Concurrent creates return unique numbers
scenarios.given: Two contributors each send a create request to one cloud-bound project at the same time
scenarios.when: When the Worker executes both reservation transactions
scenarios.then: Then each receives a distinct ticket number and no duplicate reservation row exists

scenarios.title: Idempotent key replay returns one reservation
scenarios.given: A client sends a reservation request that fails after the Worker allocated, and retries with the same Idempotency-Key and request hash
scenarios.when: When the retry reaches the Worker
scenarios.then: Then the original reservation is returned and the project counter has advanced only once

scenarios.title: Cross-project allocation is independent
scenarios.given: Two cloud projects exist with counters at different values
scenarios.when: When each project processes a create concurrently
scenarios.then: Then each allocates from its own counter and the numbers do not collide

scenarios.title: Failed local write retries the same reservation
scenarios.given: Allocation succeeds but the local Markdown write fails and the operation journal holds the reservation
scenarios.when: When the client retries create
scenarios.then: Then it reuses the same reservation id and acknowledges it without allocating a new number

scenarios.title: Coordination down blocks cloud create
scenarios.given: A cloud-bound project cannot reach the coordination service
scenarios.when: When a create is attempted
scenarios.then: Then it fails recoverably and never assigns a local fallback number, temporary key, range, or lease

scenarios.title: Outage keeps existing tickets usable
scenarios.given: The coordination service is unavailable for a cloud-bound project
scenarios.when: When a client reads or edits an existing Markdown ticket
scenarios.then: Then the operation succeeds while new cloud-bound creation stays blocked

scenarios.title: Local-only projects are unchanged
scenarios.given: A project has no cloud binding
scenarios.when: When a client creates a ticket
scenarios.then: Then allocation uses the existing local highest-plus-one scan and no cloud call is made

scenarios.title: Human email attribution on live Worker
scenarios.given: A human authenticates through Cloudflare Access and calls the coordination API
scenarios.when: When the Worker validates the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion
scenarios.then: Then it maps the verified email as a human principal and the audit records kind=human

scenarios.title: Service-token machine attribution on live Worker
scenarios.given: A headless client presents Access service-token headers
scenarios.when: When Access forwards the assertion to the Worker
scenarios.then: Then it maps the verified common_name as a machine principal and the audit records kind=machine

scenarios.title: Role permissions per project
scenarios.given: A viewer, contributor, and owner each attempt reserve, publish, list-members, and manage-members
scenarios.when: When each operation is authorized
scenarios.then: Then viewer is denied writes, contributor can reserve and publish but not manage members, and owner can do all

scenarios.title: Unknown project is non-disclosing
scenarios.given: A principal requests a project it has no membership in, and a truly nonexistent project
scenarios.when: When the Worker responds
scenarios.then: Then both return the identical 404 project_not_found with no distinguishing detail

scenarios.title: Revoked membership blocks next operation
scenarios.given: An owner revokes a member's role
scenarios.when: When that member's next request reaches the Worker
scenarios.then: Then it is denied with no authorization cache having served a stale grant

scenarios.title: Projection exposes only approved headers
scenarios.given: A ticket is acknowledged and its projection published
scenarios.when: When another client polls projections
scenarios.then: Then it receives only code, title, status, type, priority, assignee, and dates, never the body

scenarios.title: Stale projection write rejected
scenarios.given: A client publishes a projection whose expected version is older than the current version
scenarios.when: When the Worker checks the precondition
scenarios.then: Then it rejects the write and does not overwrite the newer projection

scenarios.title: Another client sees changes via polling
scenarios.given: One client publishes a status change to a projection
scenarios.when: When a second authorized client polls at the configured interval
scenarios.then: Then it observes the change within pollIntervalSeconds

scenarios.title: Board labels projected stubs
scenarios.given: A cloud-projected header exists for a ticket with no canonical local file
scenarios.when: When the board renders
scenarios.then: Then it shows a clearly labeled read-only stub that implies no teammate ownership or presence

scenarios.title: Actions produce structured redacted audit
scenarios.given: An allocation, projection update, membership change, denial, and recovery each occur
scenarios.when: When each completes
scenarios.then: Then a structured audit record is written to D1 with principal kind and id but no raw token, cookie, or assertion

scenarios.title: Disabling cloud keeps content usable
scenarios.given: A cloud-bound project is suspended and detached per the documented sequence
scenarios.when: When cloud binding is removed
scenarios.then: Then all ticket files remain readable and editable from Markdown/Git

scenarios.title: Idempotency key reused with a different request
scenarios.given: A client reuses an Idempotency-Key with a different canonical request hash
scenarios.when: When the request reaches the Worker
scenarios.then: Then it returns 409 idempotency_key_reused and allocates no new number

scenarios.title: Failed local write retries the same reservation
scenarios.given: Allocation succeeded but neither acknowledgement nor a canonical file ever appears and the reservation ages
scenarios.when: When the client retries create or the scheduled handler runs
scenarios.then: Then it reuses the same reservation id and if retired the number is never reused

scenarios.title: Human email attribution with JWKS refresh
scenarios.given: An assertion arrives with a kid absent from the cached JWKS
scenarios.when: When the verifier refreshes and the human authenticates through Access
scenarios.then: Then it maps the verified email as a human principal and refreshes JWKS once on unknown kid

scenarios.title: Service-token attribution respects origin allowlist
scenarios.given: A headless adapter is asked to send service-token headers to an origin not in cloudSync.allowedOrigins
scenarios.when: When it builds the request to obtain machine attribution
scenarios.then: Then it refuses to attach the headers and rejects any redirect

scenarios.title: Role permissions protect the final owner
scenarios.given: An attempt is made to remove or demote the last owner of a project
scenarios.when: When the Worker authorizes the membership change
scenarios.then: Then it is denied

scenarios.title: Scheduled expiry produces structured audit
scenarios.given: Reserved rows older than 24 hours exist
scenarios.when: When the 15-minute scheduled handler runs
scenarios.then: Then a bounded batch is marked abandoned and an audit record is written without decrementing the counter

obligations.title: Cloud package boundary: cloud/ owns Worker runtime; app packages reach it only via JSON/HTTPS over @mdt/domain-contracts
Access JWT validation and principal mapping: RS256 JWKS verify, human/machine principal, no secrets in config
Membership authorization: per-project roles, non-disclosure, revocation, no authz cache
Allocation transaction: static D1 batch allocates unique numbers with idempotent replay, monotonic counter, no reuse
Local orchestration: project binding selects local or durable cloud create; journal recovery; origin allowlist; local-only preserved
Versioned header projection: one-way publish, precondition conflicts, polling cursor, board distinction
Operations: migrations, scheduled maintenance, redacted audit, rate-limit abuse guard, disable/vendor-exit

testPlans.title: Allocation concurrency + uniqueness under local D1
Access JWT validation: RS256 issuer/audience/expiry principal mapping unknown kid refresh
Role enforcement viewer/contributor/owner final owner protection
Unknown vs hidden project non-disclosure revocation blocks next op
Board renders cloud stub read-only labeled non-draggable no body degraded state blocks create
Structured redacted audit for allocation projection membership denial recovery scheduled-expiry
Disabling cloud binding leaves Markdown usable operator procedure
Real human email attribution against live Access-protected Worker
Real service-token machine attribution against live Worker
Deployed concurrency scenario with latency and D1 row evidence
Apply migrations to remote D1 verify schema and FKs record bookmark
Export before restore restore export readability drill
Rate limit is abuse-only does not gate allocation correctness
Package boundary: cloud imports only domain-contracts; no app package imports @mdt/cloud
Idempotent replay returns one reservation; key reuse with different hash is 409
Cross-project allocation independence
Local write failure retries same reservation; lost acknowledgement recovers from journal
Production allocation batch preserves atomic uniqueness and monotonic counters under a forced race
Cloud-bound create has no local fallback; local-only preserved
Machine common_name maps to a machine principal
Projection exposes only approved headers and never a body
Stale expected-version is rejected and divergent conflict is not auto-merged
Polling cursor returns acknowledged projections in revision order
Cloud binding is opt-in per project; absent or disabled binding stays local
Config schema rejects tokens secrets audience tags in project and global config files
First slice ships no presence offline-allocation body-sync WebSocket or Durable Object surface
Shipped origins are trusted; custom origins are denied by default and project files cannot expand trust
TicketService durable cloud create, recovery, no fallback, local edit and status projection
Owner-only local server feed and production browser polling preserve header-only stale state
Scheduled maintenance deletes audit rows older than 180 days in bounded batches
Worker request bodies are JSON objects and size bounded; runtime failures use canonical errors

tasks.title: Slice 1: package-boundary and exclusions enforcement tests
Slice 1: Access JWT validation + principal mapping (RS256, JWKS, kid refresh)
Slice 2: static allocation batch, reservation lifecycle, idempotency, recovery
Slice 2: membership authorizer, roles, non-disclosure, revocation
UAT: register cloudSync selectors in the config-inspection registry (inspect:config --filter cloudSync returns 0 today)
UAT: prove allocation concurrency against the real D1 batch (counter pre-read outside batch today); the sync-loop test does not prove concurrent-request behavior
Wire TicketService.createCR to durable cloud orchestration while preserving local-only behavior
Implement coordination/projection HTTP clients, credentials, recovery, and safe projection retry
Acknowledge reservation and create projection v1 atomically
Enforce advisory read, mutation, and operator rate limits in Worker routes
Poll through the owner-only local server feed and render read-only projected board stubs
Shared cloud create orchestration, operation journal, credentials, config, and allowlist
Atomic initial projection, versioned publish, safe local retry, polling, and board stubs
Scheduled reservation expiry, 180-day audit retention, and rate-limit abuse guard
Versioned routing, bounded JSON validation, typed errors, request telemetry, and health route
